findings.description: pauseWithdraw() mutates totalStaked (line 602) WITHOUT calling _updatePool() first and WITHOUT calling _updatePhUSDEmissionRate() afterward. It is the only state-mutating path in the contract that does neither (verified against the full _updatePool call-site map: 242,259,362,387,408,432,622,648,695,742 — none inside 596-611; and the _updatePhUSDEmissionRate map: 245,674,725). Accrual is NOT frozen by the pause: _updatePool remains reachable while paused via the PERMISSIONLESS collectReward (618, no whenNotPaused) and the owner setters setDesiredAPY/setDepletionDuration. Exploit sequence: (1) pool paused at T0 with lastRewardTime=T0 (beginFlush at 432 does exactly this on every promo rotation); (2) time passes to T1, no _updatePool runs; (3) a whale calls pauseWithdraw, dropping totalStaked by e.g. 90% and realigning their own debts to the stale T0 accumulators (forfeiting [T0,T1] — documented intent); (4) anyone calls collectReward(1 wei), and _updatePool computes timeElapsed=T1-T0 against the STALE phUSDPerSecond (still sized for the FULL pre-exit totalStaked, because pauseWithdraw never recomputes it) and divides by the NEW reduced totalStaked at line 805. Both errors push the same direction: the surviving 10% of stakers receive the entire pool's [T0,T1] phUSD emission — a ~10x per-share over-accrual. The stable leg (792) is capped by rewardBalance so it is a redistribution, but the phUSD leg is MINTED on demand (_claimRewards:853, phUSD.mint) with no budget cap, making it an unbacked over-mint. The stale rate also persists past unpause until the next stake/withdraw. Reachable in NORMAL operation, not an exotic path: beginFlush pauses the pool for every rotation. Same class as the confirmed sibling-repo finding phoenix-nft-staking NFTStaker.emergencyWithdraw survivor over-emission, and the Linear-Depletion/rate-drift family this protocol has a recurring history with.
vulnerableWhenMet: totalStaked / share balance mutated before _updatePool() settles pending at the old rate
late/surviving staker receives accrual for a period they did not solely earn
per-call mint amount derived from accounting with no emission cap
missingMitigations: No _updatePool() at the head of pauseWithdraw
Pause does not freeze the stable/phUSD accrual legs (only the promo leg is phase-gated at 824)
findings.notes: The DEBT-FORFEIT on the exiting user is documented intent (V3 fix for the V1/V2 partial-pauseWithdraw brick) — that is NOT the finding. The finding is the un-settled window being redistributed to survivors at an inflated per-share rate. Possible relationship to the V3-Q-02 'trap warning' in the run-08 ledger (the obvious fix strands funds): a naive fix that settles accrual inside pauseWithdraw must not resurrect the underflow brick the debt realignment was added to fix. Windfall accrues passively to existing survivors; an attacker cannot enter during pause (stake is whenNotPaused), so this is value-leak/over-mint rather than a directable theft — severity-classifier should weigh that.

findings.description: collectReward() is PERMISSIONLESS (external nonReentrant, only require(amount > 0) — no auth, no minimum amount) and unconditionally re-anchors the depletion schedule: rewardPerSecond = (rewardBalance * PRECISION) / depletionDuration (line 629). Every call restarts a fresh FULL depletionDuration window over the entire remaining balance. Anyone can call collectReward(1) with 1 wei of rewardToken. Repeated calls convert the intended LINEAR depletion (balance fully distributed at t=D) into EXPONENTIAL decay (dB/dt = -B/D), so only ~63% is distributed after D and the stream never completes — stable rewards are asymptotically withheld from stakers for the cost of 1 wei plus gas per call. This is the V1 Linear-Depletion rate-recompute bug class NOT removed but RELOCATED: the V2 fix (documented at _updatePool:797) removed the recompute from _updatePool, yet left it at collectReward, which is a permissionless entry point. The intended caller is the yield-accumulator delivering real yield; nothing enforces that. Note the same re-anchor exists at the promo mirror (topUpPromotion:394, setPromoDepletionDuration:412) but those are onlyOwner, so they are at most an owner footgun, not a griefing vector.
vulnerableWhenMet: recompute pushes the effective window end forward and applies it to already-elapsed/remaining balance
emission schedule re-anchored by an unprivileged caller
missingMitigations: No rate-limit / cooldown on the re-anchor
No preservation of the original window end
findings.notes: Operator memory explicitly records the Linear-Depletion bug as REPORTABLE for this project and directs it not to be re-suppressed. Legit high-frequency small collectReward calls stretch the schedule even with no attacker. Likely Medium downstream (griefing / DoS of reward delivery, no theft) — severity-classifier to adjudicate; recorded here at the pattern's own HIGH mapping.

findings.description: _tryTransfer returns `callSuccess && (returndata.length == 0 || abi.decode(returndata, (bool)))`. A raw .call to a CODELESS address returns success=true with empty returndata, so the helper reports TRUE for a transfer that never happened — in PhlimboV3.batchClaim (471) that records a promo payment as paid and aligns promoDebt, erasing the entitlement with nothing banked; in MigratorV2V3._forward (362) it returns early without banking. Confirmed divergence from OZ SafeERC20: OZ routes through Address, which checks `target.code.length > 0` (Address.sol:143) and reverts AddressEmptyCode; _tryTransfer omits precisely that check. DUPLICATION STATUS (explicitly checked per task): the two copies are BYTE-IDENTICAL — md5 of PhlimboV3.sol:885-889 == md5 of MigratorV2V3.sol:350-354 (27d9d3e6b52b4d6aafb53d9d79caf546). The 7045a96..02b9bc2 diff shows story-028 ADDED the MigratorV2V3 copy as a fresh duplicate of the existing defect, and touched the PhlimboV3 copy only to rejoin a wrapped line (formatting, no semantic change). So neither copy was fixed — there is no one-fixed-one-missed divergence, but the defect surface has DOUBLED and any future fix must land in both.
vulnerableWhenMet: Return bool not checked against the codeless-target case (no require/assert on target having code)
findings.reachabilityBarrier: The token address, not the recipient, must be codeless for the false-success. In PhlimboV3 promoToken is installed only via startPromotion (365) whose safeTransferFrom would itself revert AddressEmptyCode on a codeless token; MigratorV2V3's tokens are the immutable phUSD/rewardToken plus V3's vetted promoToken. Post-Cancun, deployed code cannot be removed. So the defect is real and certain in the code but its exploit path is currently blocked by the install-time barrier — which is why this reconciles to the existing open Low V3-L-10 rather than escalating. Flagged as still-live, NOT re-severitized.

manualReview.description: abi.decode(returndata, (bool)) REVERTS on a non-empty returndata shorter than 32 bytes. Inside PhlimboV3.batchClaim the revert propagates out of the whole loop, permanently pinning flushCursor at the offending staker: finalizePromotion requires flushCursor == _stakers.length() (513), so the promo rotation can never complete. CONTAINMENT ASYMMETRY (the notable part): the byte-identical MigratorV2V3 copy is defended — _forward runs inside migrateOne, which migrate wraps in try/catch (202-211), and the owner has skipCurrent (284) as a cursor backstop. PhlimboV3.batchClaim has NEITHER an outer try/catch NOR any cursor-skip. The same helper is therefore fail-safe in the migrator and fail-brick in the farm. Owner can abortFlush (539) to unpin the contract, so the pool is not bricked — only the rotation is, and re-running beginFlush hits the same staker again.
manualReview.reachabilityBarrier: A short-returning promoToken cannot be installed: startPromotion's safeTransferFrom (365) routes through OZ SafeERC20, whose own abi.decode would revert on the same short return. Requires a token that returns 32 bytes for transferFrom but short data for transfer, or an upgradeable token that changes behaviour post-install — speculative. Routed to manualReview rather than dropped: this is the existing open V3-L-02, and the containment asymmetry vs the migrator copy is new information worth a human look.

manualReview.description: pauseWithdraw is the ONLY user-facing state-mutating function without nonReentrant (stake:643, withdraw:688, claim:738, collectReward:618, batchClaim:450, claimUnclaimablePromo:561 all carry it). It mutates user.amount, totalStaked and all three debts. batchClaim calls out to the owner-chosen promoToken via _tryTransfer mid-loop (471), and _claimRewards transfers promoToken (873) BEFORE its callers write debts (stake:664, withdraw:710, claim:757) — a CEI violation that is currently saved only by the shared OZ v5 lock. No profitable path found: stake/withdraw/claim are whenNotPaused while pauseWithdraw is whenPaused, so they cannot overlap; and a reentrant pauseWithdraw during batchClaim realigns debts against an accPromoPerShare that is frozen during Flushing (824), leaving pending==0 — consistent. Surfaced because the guard omission is real and the protection is incidental rather than designed; a future change to the phase gate or the whenNotPaused set could turn this live.

manualReview.type: two-step setter with no minimum delay
manualReview.description: setDesiredAPY's two-step commit has an UPPER bound (block.number > pendingAPYBlockNumber + 100 re-arms a preview) but NO LOWER bound: preview and commit can occur in the same block/transaction, so the two-step provides no timelock or observation window — it only guards against a single fat-fingered call. Step 2 correctly compares the passed bps against the snapshotted pendingAPYBps rather than re-reading a live value, and the commit branch correctly _updatePool()s at the old rate (242) before _updatePhUSDEmissionRate() (245), so the accrual-ordering leg of this pattern is NOT vulnerable. Owner-only, and the transparency limitation is arguably obvious → likely Law-3 trusted rather than a footgun. Routed for adjudication, not asserted.

seedUsers does `delete users` (148) then push-loops the new list (149-151). The delete costs gas proportional to the PREVIOUS pass's length, so a large first pass (e.g. 10k addresses) could make the reseed for a small straggler list OOG — the straggler pass is the documented mitigation for users who re-enter V2 after their index was processed, so bricking it would strand those users in V2. Owner-controlled input on both legs and chunkable in practice by seeding smaller lists; migrate/batchClaim themselves are properly chunked via maxIterations. Low, surfaced for completeness.

noMatchRationale.FIRST-DEPOSITOR-ATTACK: MINIMUM_STAKE = 1e15 (164) enforced at stake:644; no share-price mechanic (fixed-denomination accumulator farm, not a vault).
noMatchRationale.ERC4626-INFLATION: Not a vault; no shares/totalAssets conversion.
noMatchRationale.FEE-ON-TRANSFER-ACCOUNTING: notVulnerableWhen satisfied: startPromotion:366 and topUpPromotion:391 both measure the balance delta and require strict equality, rejecting FoT/rebasing tokens by policy. MigratorV2V3.migrateOne uses balance-delta bracketing (243-264) rather than crediting requested amounts.
noMatchRationale.ROUNDING-DIRECTION: Accumulator arithmetic rounds DOWN via integer division on both the accrual leg (792/805/829) and the debt leg, i.e. against the user; no ceil/floor asymmetry and no round-trip conversion pair.
noMatchRationale.REENTRANCY-ERC721-RECEIVE: No ERC721/1155 surface in this project.
noMatchRationale.REENTRANCY-READONLY: Views (pendingPhUSD/pendingStable/pendingPromo, getPoolInfo) report per-user entitlements, not a price/exchange-rate consumed as an oracle by integrators. pendingPromo:955 correctly mirrors _updatePool's Flushing phase gate.
noMatchRationale.WEAK-PRNG: block.timestamp is used for time-based accrual only, no value-bearing random outcome.
noMatchRationale.INCORRECT-OPERATOR: Boundary checks reviewed: finalizePromotion's strict `flushCursor == _stakers.length()` (513) is reachable because batchClaim caps the cursor at len (456-458); the +100 block window at 234 has no value consequence. No off-by-one with consequence found.
noMatchRationale.TIMELOCK-BYPASS: No timelock construct in scope (see PATTERN-006 for the related no-minimum-delay observation).
